subject: Archaeology
title: Pompeii: Frozen in Ash
description: A quick win: understand Pompeii: Frozen in Ash.

hook.text: In 79 CE, Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried an entire Roman city under 20 feet of volcanic ash.

buildup.text: Pompeii vanished from memory for 1,700 years until workers accidentally found it in 1748.

discovery.text: The ash preserved everything: bread in ovens, graffiti on walls, and even the shapes of fleeing people.

twist.text: Archaeologist Fiorelli poured plaster into the voids left by bodies, creating haunting human casts.

climax.text: Pompeii gave us the most complete picture of daily Roman life ever found — a city frozen in time.

punchline.text: A disaster that killed thousands gave us a window into how they lived.

quiz.question: How did archaeologist Fiorelli reveal the shapes of Pompeii's victims?
options: He used X-ray technology to scan the ash layers
He poured plaster into the voids left by decomposed bodies
He reconstructed them from skeletal remains using clay

details.summary: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE buried Pompeii under meters of volcanic ash, preserving an entire Roman city — streets, shops, temples, homes, food, graffiti, and even human bodies — in extraordinary detail. Excavations since the 1700s have revealed daily Roman life.
details.whyItMatters: No other archaeological site preserves an ancient city so completely. Pompeii provides an unmatched snapshot of Roman daily life — from food on tables to election slogans on walls — that no text or ruin elsewhere can match.
takeaways: Vesuvius buried Pompeii under volcanic ash in 79 CE
The city was preserved with streets, shops, and human remains
It is the most complete picture of daily Roman life available

faq.question: How were human bodies preserved at Pompeii?
faq.answer: Bodies decomposed inside cavities in the hardened ash. In the 1860s, Giuseppe Fiorelli injected plaster into these voids, creating casts that capture victims' final moments — their postures, clothing folds, and facial expressions frozen at the instant of death.

faq.question: How much of Pompeii has been excavated?
faq.answer: About two-thirds of the city has been uncovered. The remaining third is deliberately left unexcavated, preserved for future archaeologists with better techniques. Current work focuses on conservation of exposed areas and targeted excavation of specific research questions.
